name: hhar
paper_title: Smart Devices are Different: Assessing and Mitigating Mobile Sensing Heterogeneities for Activity Recognition
authors: Allan Stisen, Henrik Blunck, Sourav Bhattacharya, Thor Siiger Prentow, Mikkel Baun Kjaergaard, Anind Dey, Tobias Sonne, Mads Moller Jensen
venue: Proceedings of the 13th ACM Conference on Embedded Networked Sensor Systems (SenSys '15), Seoul, Republic of Korea, pp. 127-140
license: Dataset: CC BY 4.0 (UCI ML Repository, DOI 10.24432/C5689X). Paper: (c) 2015 ACM; accepted manuscript openly available via Aarhus University Pure.
notes: This is the ORIGINAL paper for the HHAR (Heterogeneity Human Activity Recognition) dataset. Data collected with 36 smartphones/smartwatches spanning 13 device models from 4 manufacturers. Sensors: accelerometer + gyroscope, sampled at each device's HIGHEST available rate (rates therefore differ across devices, a deliberate 'heterogeneity' feature of the dataset; commonly ~50-200 Hz depending on device). 6 activities: Biking, Sitting, Standing, Walking, Stair Up, Stair Down. 9 subjects performed a scripted 5-min-per-activity workload with phones (8 phones) in a waist pouch and watches (4 watches) on the arms. Total ~43.9M sensor readings. Raw CSV columns: Index, Arrival_Time, Creation_Time, x, y, z, User, Model, Device, gt(=activity label). UCI dataset DOI: 10.24432/C5689X. PDF is the accepted manuscript captured from Aarhus University Pure via the Wayback Machine (2017-08-08 snapshot, full 5.35MB, ends in %%EOF); the live pure.au.dk copy is behind a Cloudflare challenge and the 2019 Wayback snapshot is truncated at 1MB.
